title: Predictive Structure Behind Rare Outcomes in Random Quantum Circuits
abstract: Local random quantum circuits can occasionally produce unusually large output probabilities. However, the final output distribution containing such a peak does not by itself reveal how the peak formed during circuit evolution. We investigate whether states formed during circuit evolution carry structural signatures that predict subsequent peak formation. In numerical experiments, circuits selected for large terminal peaks exhibit stronger pairwise correlations and probability redistribution, together with lower bipartite entanglement and output entropy, than controls generated by the same random-circuit model. Their intermediate states retain higher fresh-peak event probability when the remaining gates are independently regenerated. Within an unconditioned ensemble, a fixed structural score computed from the initial circuit segment predicts new-peak probability. Averaged equally across n=8-16, a replay with equal numbers of remaining-circuit evaluations shows that score-based allocation yields 1.80 times as many peaks as uniform allocation and about 18% more than a fixed baseline based on probability concentration and redistribution. Randomizing relative phases while preserving computational-basis probabilities strongly attenuates the selected-state advantage, demonstrating a functional contribution from relative-phase organization. Controlled gate-selection tests further show that the identified structure can guide circuit construction to promote peak formation. Together, these results connect rare output events to intermediate-state structure with predictive and constructive value under finite-depth local dynamics.

bite.hook: Score-based allocation yields 1.80 times as many rare output peaks in random quantum circuits than uniform allocation.
tldr: Investigated whether intermediate states in random quantum circuits contain structural signatures that predict rare output peaks.
Analyzed numerical experiments on circuits to track pairwise correlations, entanglement, and probability redistribution.
Found that structural scores successfully predict new-peak probabilities and generate significantly more peaks than baseline methods.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding how rare outcomes form in quantum circuits helps scientists control quantum systems better, paving the way for more efficient quantum computing algorithms.
bite.eli5: If you shake a box of dice a million times, you occasionally get a rare winning roll. Scientists found a way to look at how the dice tumble halfway through the shake to predict when a lucky roll is coming.
